### Renamed

- `--ds-vert` → `--ds-vert` — Value corrected #89fc79 -> #53ff64. The 0.11 hex was eye-dropped from the charter PNG on the belief that the swatch label was a typo; the label was right. Name unchanged — re-check any hard-coded copy of the old hex. (batch 0.3)
- `--ds-accent (in charts, sparkline, bar-chart series)` → `--ds-chart-1` — Data series no longer read the themeable accent. Visually identical at the default theme (--ds-chart-1 is #ff2a00); a theme that overrode --ds-accent to recolour its charts must now override --ds-chart-*. (batch 0.3)
- `Wordmark ({ name, sub })` → `Wordmark ({ variant, label, name, sub })` — The geometric construction 0.x drew — a circle, a square and a diagonal line, the brand's three elements as primitives — is replaced by the produced lockups, as two `currentColor` variants: `horizontal` (the full name) and `square` (the monogram). `name` and `sub` are unchanged and still render `.ds-wordmark__name` / `__sub`, but they no longer default: a bare <Wordmark /> is now the lockup alone, where it used to print the word "Diametral". A name beside the mark wants variant="square" — the horizontal lockup already spells it. `.ds-wordmark__mark` still styles a hand-written svg; the React binding emits none. `assets/logo/diametral-mark.svg` still holds the geometric mark and has not been re-cut to match. (batch 3)
- `.ds-wordmark, .ds-wordmark__mark, .ds-wordmark__name, .ds-wordmark__sub (in app-bar.css)` → `.ds-wordmark, .ds-wordmark__mark, .ds-wordmark__name, .ds-wordmark__sub (in wordmark.css)` — File move only, no rename and no visual change — the four rules left app-bar.css for the new wordmark.css when the real lockup landed. Anyone importing css/diametral.css is unaffected; only a consumer cherry-picking css/components/app-bar.css has to add css/components/wordmark.css. (batch 3)
- `.ds-button-group (in button-extras.css)` → `.ds-button-group (in button-group.css)` — Replaced wholesale, same name. The seam no longer overlaps members with margin-left: -1px; it removes the losing border with border-inline-start-width, which is identical in LTR and correct in RTL. Every selector matches both the new parts' data-slot and .ds-button/.ds-input/.ds-select, so existing markup keeps joining. New: [data-orientation="vertical"], .ds-button-group-text and .ds-button-group-separator. (batch 3)
- `IconButton ({ size: "sm" | "lg" })` → `IconButton ({ size: "icon" | "icon-xs" | "icon-sm" | "icon-lg" | "xs" | "sm" | "lg" })` — Additive, not a rename: `sm` and `lg` keep working, and `icon-` is simply stripped, so the source's four square spellings resolve onto the same boxes. `icon-xs` (24px, .ds-button--xs) is new. `label` was already required on both sides — the ledger's "incumbent is a class-applier" premise does not hold here, the same way batch-plan §1.1 found for stat-card. Moved from react/components/ButtonExtras.tsx to react/components/icon-button.tsx; the barrel import is unchanged. (batch 3)
- `GaugeChart, GaugeChartProps, GaugeChartThreshold` → `Gauge, GaugeThreshold` — Renamed with the absorption; every prop survives (`value`, `max`, `size`, `thickness`, `label`, `color`, `thresholds`, `format`) and the props interface is gone in favour of the inline type, the way every absorbed component declares its props. A find-and-replace of the symbol is the whole migration. (batch 4)
- `LineChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })` → `LineChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey })` — Recharts replaced the hand-rolled SVG, so a series is named and coloured once in `config` — one entry per key in each `data` row — and the rows are objects rather than parallel arrays. `labels` becomes `xAxisKey`, the row field holding them; `width`/`height` become the container's box (`.ds-chart-container--plot`, retuned with `--ds-chart-height`). `grid` and `dots` are unchanged. Same for AreaChart, which additionally gains `stacked`. (batch 4)
- `AreaChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })` → `AreaChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey, stacked })` — See LineChart. `stacked` is new: two areas drawn over each other are usually meant to sum. (batch 4)
- `BarChart ({ data: BarChartDatum[] })` → `BarChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey, statusKey, max, horizontal, stacked })` — 0.11 took one array of `{ label, value, status }`; the rows are now recharts rows and the measure is a `config` key. `status` moves from the datum to `statusKey`, a row field naming the tone, and all six 0.11 tones survive (success, warning, danger, critical, neutral, info) — the source's own map had only four. `horizontal` and `max` keep their 0.11 names and meaning. BarChartDatum is gone. (batch 4)
- `StackedBar ({ segments, showLegend })` → `StackedBar ({ config, data, labelKey, showLegend })` — Still the share chart: each row is normalised to its own total. `segments` and their colours become `config`; the row label becomes `labelKey`. For raw magnitudes rather than shares, use BarChart with `stacked`. (batch 4)
- `PieChart ({ data, color, legend, size })` → `PieChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, legend })` — `valueKey`/`nameKey` name the row fields; a slice's colour is a `config` entry keyed by its name, which is also how the tooltip and legend find its label. `size` becomes the container's square box — retune it with `--ds-chart-height`. (batch 4)
- `DonutChart ({ data, centerLabel, thickness, legend, size })` → `DonutChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, centerLabel, centerCaption, thickness, legend })` — See PieChart. `thickness` is now a percentage of the chart radius, not px, because the container is responsive and a px ring would not scale with it. `centerCaption` is new: the uppercase line under the figure, in the register Gauge uses. - `Sparkline (flat series drawn along the floor)` → `Sparkline (flat series pinned to the middle)` — Props are unchanged. - `.ds-chart-legend__value` → _removed_ — Removed with the chart merge. Print the figure in the tooltip (`.ds-chart-tooltip-content-item-value`), or beside the chart as prose. (batch 4)

- `Switch `children` / `onChange`` → `Label + `onCheckedChange`` — Same shape change as Checkbox: the root is the track, and its name is a `<Label htmlFor>` beside it. (batch 7)
- `Tag `status`` → `tone` — Widened from four values to the same six every other status surface takes. `status` is still accepted and still maps. (batch 7)
- `Icon `strokeWidth`` → _removed_ — Accepted and ignored since the set became Phosphor: filled geometry has no stroke to widen. Still accepted rather than removed, because removing it costs a caller a build for no gain. (batch 7)
- `IconButton / SpeedDial / ToolbarButton `variant`` → `the full eight-value `ButtonVariant`` — Widened, not renamed: these narrowed to `primary | danger` while they were composed onto the incumbent Button. The second half of batches 1, 3 and 6's forward cross-batch imports. (batch 7)
- `.ds-card-content (source spelling)` → `.ds-card__body` — The absorbed part is renamed into the frozen grammar: `__body` is what this system already called that region. (batch 7)
- `.ds-card-header / -title / -footer (source spelling)` → `.ds-card__header / __title / __footer` — Renamed into the frozen BEM grammar `Card.js` and `docs/components.md` already taught. (batch 7)
- `.ds-panel-header / -title / -content / -footer / -row (source spelling)` → `.ds-panel__header / __title / __content / __footer / __row` — Same rename. `__title` is what `<ds-panel title>` writes, so it is a contract and the other four follow it. (batch 7)
- `.ds-input (defined in field.css)` → `.ds-input (defined in input.css)` — Declarations moved file, name unchanged. Four stylesheets override it by descent — `color-picker.css`, `time-picker.css`, `date-picker.css`, `date-range.css` — and all four win on specificity, so none of them moved. (batch 7)
- `.ds-checkbox / .ds-textarea / .ds-select / .ds-range / .ds-input-group (defined in form-controls.css)` → `the same names, in checkbox.css / textarea.css / select.css / slider.css / input-group.css` — `form-controls.css` split seven ways and kept only the radio block. Every class name is unchanged; only the file it lives in moved. `.ds-field--error`, `.ds-field--success` and `.ds-field__hint` moved to `field.css`. (batch 7)
- `.ds-agenda-event-status--info / --success / --warning / --danger / --critical` → `.ds-status--info / --success / --warning / --danger / --critical` — The agenda's status dot is a `<Status><StatusIndicator/>` now, so its six private tone rules left `agenda.css`. One status is one colour system-wide. (batch 7)
- `<svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">` → `<svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 256 256" fill="currentColor">` — Lucide -> Phosphor. Every icon **name** is unchanged, so no `<Icon>` or `<ds-icon>` call moves; hand-written `<svg class="ds-icon">` does, because the wrapper attributes and the geometry both change. (batch 7)
